paper_metadata.title: Semi-coherent nanoprecipitates induced by Nb microalloying enable high-strength and hydrogen-resistant interstitial high-entropy alloy

evidence.quote: the semi-coherent carbide/matrix interface in Nb-microalloyed FeMnCoCr-C interstitial high-entropy alloy (iHEA) can simultaneously improve the strength and HE resistance.

evidence.section: 2.3 Tensile testing under in-situ electrochemical hydrogen charging
evidence.quote: The CoCrFeMnNi (at.%) HEA, which was prepared by using the same process, was also tested to compare the HE resistance.
The ingots with a nominal chemical composition of Fe(49.5-x)Mn30Co10Cr10C0.5-Nbx (at.%, x = 0, 0.05) were prepared by vacuum arc melting under the protection of high pure Ar for at least five times.
The as-cast ingots were then hot rolled at 1,000 ℃ to a thickness reduction of 50%
followed by homogenization annealing at 1,200 ℃ for 2 h and quenching in water.
followed by homogenization annealing at 1,200 ℃ for 2 h and quenching in water.
Subsequently, the homogenized plates were cold rolled to a thickness reduction of 50%.
To achieve full recrystallization and precipitation of NbC, the recrystallization annealing treatment was performed at 850 ℃ for 30 min.

evidence.quote: Nb microalloying remarkably increases the YS (695 MPa) and UTS (1,049 MPa) when tested in air.
the nano-sized NbC can effectively inhibit grain growth during recrystallization annealing and refine the grain of the 0.05Nb iHEA by pinning the dislocations and GBs
the cores of misfit dislocations at the interface of NbC and the matrix are the deep hydrogen trapping sites
This phenomenon has been associated with the hydrogen-enhanced decohesion (HEDE) mechanism, that is, the presence of hydrogen can reduce the cohesive strength of GBs
the precipitation of NbC particles and grain refinement restrain the dislocation slip, rather than the nucleation of dislocations
